scores.why: A provides the strongest evidence-led disposition register, migration checks, redirects and cutover controls; B covers inventory, import and tested redirects with an estimate but gives weaker content-verification detail; C concentrates on an existing-AEM migration despite Drupal being specified; D supplies a useful non-AEM import and redirect method but lacks comparable retained-content validation, effort and scheduling commitments.

A and B offer equivalent generic inventory, metadata import and reconciliation plans but omit duplicate resolution, revision controls, mandatory fields and engineer approval; C adds taxonomy and metadata design while still missing those controls and introducing unexplained Content Hub scope; D directly addresses hashes, superseded manuals, required fields, engineer sign-off, staged loading and reconciliation with clear responsibilities and effort.

A principally builds reusable templates without migrating preferences or proving suppression; B combines programme rebuilding, suppression flags and actual first-send recipient checks but leaves timing and conflict precedence underdeveloped; C supplies explicit restrictive conflict rules, unmatched suppression handling, reconciliation and a launch gate while leaving flag enforcement and preference-sync behaviour uncertain; D gives concrete import and flag controls with an estimate but omits programme rebuilding and relies on weaker internal test-recipient evidence.

A describes generic setup, sync and lifecycle work without an enquiry-routing design; B identifies Salesforce territory ownership, existing-record matching, mapping, fallback review and effort but leaves repeated submissions, territory changes and failure detection insufficiently specified; C and D provide substantively equivalent data-hygiene and scoring plans with deliverables and estimates yet do not resolve the requested routing and unanswered-enquiry cases.

A, B and D address AI-referred audience activation instead of defining and collecting the requested events, with B also introducing an unnecessary dependency that includes a prohibited new CDP; C defines the three events, market dimensions, payload restrictions and test outputs with timing and effort, but does not explain collection mechanics or expected-count reconciliation and leaves its claim about sensitive-field labels enforcing analytical restrictions uncertain.

A best preserves Power BI through a signed metric dictionary, CJA data views, explicit entitlement and data-movement assumptions, effort and reconciliation outputs, although Salesforce comparisons need more detail; B offers a plausible BI-extension connection and entitlement but little metric governance or delivery commitment; C and D offer equivalent dashboard briefs, measure guides, checks and estimates, yet primarily reconcile Power BI with CJA rather than explaining disputed web-versus-sales totals.

A offers generic discovery without an accessibility assessment or remediation method; B and C provide equivalent WCAG 2.2 AA template work, automated and manual tests and author guidance but omit published-document treatment and completion verification ownership; D adds multilingual component testing, form checks, document sampling and fix-and-retest evidence, although its reviewer remains a placeholder and optional document remediation leaves full published-document acceptance unresolved.

A and D provide similarly narrow AEM Sites release, log-review and reporting services while omitting the other products, integration ownership and fee boundaries; B covers all four products, incident triage, integrations, routine changes, reporting, twelve-month effort and separately estimated work, although service levels and monitoring coverage need completion; C covers useful monthly activities across all four products but lacks comparable incident ownership, integration scope, effort, duration and commercial boundaries.

notes: Context quotations, headings and answer position earned no independent credit, and answers with equivalent substantive coverage received equal scores.

The strongest answers turned client requirements into specific controls, approval evidence and bounded delivery commitments; generic product descriptions and unrelated capabilities scored poorly even when technically plausible.

Adobe assertions were assessed only from the supplied panel, so cross-record suppression, bidirectional preference behaviour and sensitive-field enforcement are treated as implementation uncertainties rather than established factual errors.

Material remaining gaps include repeated-enquiry and territory-change behaviour, reconciliation against Salesforce totals, complete published-document accessibility acceptance and contracted incident service levels.

All answers were treated as within the displayed word limits, and an additional entitlement was not automatically penalized; relevance, explanation and consistency with the client's purchasing constraints determined its significance.
